findings.criterion: cross-cutting security/data integrity — idempotency on required CRUD writes
findings.issue: useSubmitKey retains one key until success but never binds or rotates it when the user deliberately changes the request payload or target after an attempted submission. If the first request committed and its response was lost, editing any field and retrying sends the stored key with a different body; defineRoute then returns idempotency_key_reuse. Error handling retains the same key, so subsequent corrected retries remain stuck until remount.
findings.consequence: A normal lost-response-then-edit workflow can make unit/site/zone/slot/person creation impossible in the current form despite the original write having succeeded.
findings.correction: Track the request target plus a canonical payload fingerprint with the submission key; reuse the key only for an exact retry and rotate before sending when the target or payload is deliberately changed. Add a rendered lost-response test that edits the payload and proves the retry uses a new key and does not enter a permanent 422 loop.

findings.criterion: 6 and cross-cutting data integrity — usable local-auth person creation
findings.issue: In local-auth mode, addPerson creates an account and returns its only temporary password, but replaySafe stores that field as null. After a committed request whose response is lost, the replay returns 201 with no credential and People displays users.invited even though no invitation exists. No password-reset/recovery path exists in apps, and the new API test explicitly accepts the missing replay credential instead of proving usable onboarding.
findings.consequence: The new person exists and consumes the requested membership, but neither the administrator nor the person has a usable credential; the UI falsely reports an invitation and the account is stranded.
findings.correction: Do not persist or replay the raw one-time password. Replace local new-user creation with a recoverable invitation/password-setup flow or add an explicit credential-recovery action and return an accurate replay state; add a lost-response UI/API test proving the person can actually complete sign-in.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting security/data integrity — idempotent Super Admin cross-property writes
findings.issue: POST /v1/platform/tenants/:slug/members still uses definePlatformRoute, which has no idempotency handling. People sends a submission key, but this endpoint ignores it. The busy flag prevents only concurrent clicks; after a committed response is lost, retry reaches addPerson again and returns already_member, with the same unrecoverable temporary-password problem for a new local user. The rendered test mocks post success and checks only that a key argument was supplied.
findings.consequence: Super Admin cross-property person creation can report failure after success and strand a newly created local account, so the cross-property write is not replay-safe.
findings.correction: Add tenant-scoped replay handling to the platform member route (including target path/body hashing), while using the recoverable onboarding response described above. Execute a same-key lost-response retry against the real platform endpoint and assert one account, membership and audit plus a usable onboarding outcome.

findings.criterion: 1 — resident can generate and share a usable, tamper-protected two-hour pass
findings.issue: No new evidence closes review iteration 09: pass-e2e still starts from a fabricated TOKEN, mounts GuestPass directly, and mocks lookup/redeem. It does not execute resident generation/share, the actual unauthenticated /pass bootstrap through AppProvider, or server HMAC, verify-code, version and expiry validation for the rendered artifact.
findings.consequence: The supplied verification does not establish that the artifact a resident actually sends survives the real public route and is accepted by the gate as that same live two-hour pass.
findings.correction: Issue a live pass through the API, invoke the real resident Share control, open its fragment URL through /pass at a mobile viewport, decode the rendered QR, and perform real lookup/redeem; assert exact token identity, two-hour expiry, and HMAC plus verify-code tamper rejection.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera plate scanning during check-in and check-out
findings.issue: No new evidence closes review iteration 09: the rendered tests replace LiveCamera with a button that emits an already-decoded plate. getUserMedia, the shipped ONNX/model loader and decoder, a camera fixture, and responsive browser behavior remain unexecuted; the existing fake-camera browser story has no recorded run and covers check-in only.
findings.consequence: Actual camera acquisition and plate decoding in the shipped stack remain unverified for both attendant flows.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 fake-camera check-in story with the real model and .y4m fixture, add and run the equivalent checkout story, and assert the visible plate, checkout match request/result, browser/model/fixture versions, and a clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete Admin CRUD and Super Admin operations across properties
findings.issue: The expanded rendered test completes CRUD only for a unit. It creates but does not edit/delete a person; creates site/zone/slot but does not edit or retire site/zone, does not edit a slot, and deletes only an existing mocked slot. Its Super Admin case performs only a mocked person POST in the second property, not the required operations across entities. Setting window.innerWidth in jsdom does not execute layout or establish mobile usability.
findings.consequence: Complete person/building/slot CRUD, Super Admin operations across buildings, and mobile behavior remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Drive create/read/edit/delete or retire for person, site, unit and slot through the real routed screens and real API at a narrow browser viewport. Switch a Super Admin to a second property and perform representative unit/site/slot/person writes there, asserting persisted results and regular-admin cross-property denial.
